mol43: Can screens permanently damage my eyes?
mol44: No. The American Academy of Ophthalmology says the idea that long screen use permanently harms the eyes is a myth. However, long periods at a screen can cause temporary discomfort such as blurred vision, aching and dryness.
mol46: In a study of 11 middle-aged and older adults, 8 hours of sitting were broken up with different break patterns. Only 5 minutes of light walking every 30 minutes significantly reduced the rise in blood sugar; this pattern also lowered systolic blood pressure by about 4 mmHg. All the break patterns tested, including 1 minute of walking every hour, lowered systolic blood pressure. As this was a small study, the results should be interpreted with caution.
mol47: Does it work if the tab is in the background?
mol48: It works as long as the page stays open. Some browsers slow down timers in background tabs, so the reminder may be delayed by a few seconds to a minute. If you allow notifications, you’ll see the reminder even while working in another window.
mol49: What can I do on a break?
mol50: Walk at an easy pace, go up and down the stairs, take a phone call standing up or do a few stretches. The World Health Organization recommends replacing sitting time with movement of any intensity.
